# FTA Census Map

FTA has created an interactive map to view the U.S. Census Bureau's designated Urban Areas, NTD Reporters, and other relevant data. The map includes both 2020 and 2010 Census data and can be used as a resource for NTD reporters, data users, and transit industry stakeholders.

**Access the Census Map**

[FTA Census Map:](https://usdot.maps.arcgis.com/apps/mapviewer/index.html?webmap=5287ba87422448c7a97e5d60cc5e4f7b) Access the Census Map here via Esri's ArcGIS Online Map Viewer tool.

**Using the Census Map**

[Interactive Census Map Access Guide:](https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/30a638acd8364c96ad13782c748742be)An interactive guide to using the FTA Census Map to aid in NTD reporting. This guide includes an introduction to navigating the map, changing the visibility of data layers on the map, and using the map for B-15 reporting purposes.

[Static Census Map Access Guide:](https://www.transit.dot.gov/ntd/fta-census-map-access-guide) A static, text-based guide to using the FTA Census Map. This guide includes screenshots.

**Map Details and Data**

[FTA Census Map Information:](https://usdot.maps.arcgis.com/home/item.html?id=5287ba87422448c7a97e5d60cc5e4f7b) Find details about the FTA Census Map here, including downloadable data layers, view count, and creation/update dates.

_The FTA Census Map layers have been updated as of November 2025 with the most recent 2024 Agency Information data._

**Additional Census Resources**

Publications such as the [2020 Census Changes UZA/Population File](https://www.transit.dot.gov/ntd/2020-census-changes-uzapopulation), webinars on the impacts of the 2020 Census on NTD Reporting, and Census FAQs can be found here on FTA's [Census Updates](https://www.transit.dot.gov/ntd/census-updates) page.

# FTA Census Map

FTA has created an interactive map to view the U.S. Census Bureau's designated Urban Areas, NTD Reporters, and other relevant data. The map includes both 2020 and 2010 Census data and can be used as a resource for NTD reporters, data users, and transit industry stakeholders.

**Access the Census Map**

[FTA Census Map:](https://usdot.maps.arcgis.com/apps/mapviewer/index.html?webmap=5287ba87422448c7a97e5d60cc5e4f7b) Access the Census Map here via Esri's ArcGIS Online Map Viewer tool.

**Using the Census Map**

[Interactive Census Map Access Guide:](https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/30a638acd8364c96ad13782c748742be)An interactive guide to using the FTA Census Map to aid in NTD reporting. This guide includes an introduction to navigating the map, changing the visibility of data layers on the map, and using the map for B-15 reporting purposes.

[Static Census Map Access Guide:](https://www.transit.dot.gov/ntd/fta-census-map-access-guide) A static, text-based guide to using the FTA Census Map. This guide includes screenshots.

**Map Details and Data**

[FTA Census Map Information:](https://usdot.maps.arcgis.com/home/item.html?id=5287ba87422448c7a97e5d60cc5e4f7b) Find details about the FTA Census Map here, including downloadable data layers, view count, and creation/update dates.

_The FTA Census Map layers have been updated as of November 2025 with the most recent 2024 Agency Information data._

**Additional Census Resources**

Publications such as the [2020 Census Changes UZA/Population File](https://www.transit.dot.gov/ntd/2020-census-changes-uzapopulation), webinars on the impacts of the 2020 Census on NTD Reporting, and Census FAQs can be found here on FTA's [Census Updates](https://www.transit.dot.gov/ntd/census-updates) page.

**Oberlin** is a town in and the [parish seat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parish_seat "Parish seat") of [Allen Parish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allen_Parish,_Louisiana "Allen Parish, Louisiana"), [Louisiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana "Louisiana"), United States.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oberlin,_Louisiana#cite_note-GR6-3) As of the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), Oberlin had a population of 1,402.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oberlin,_Louisiana#cite_note-Census2020PLLede-4) The town is named after [Johann Friedrich Oberlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johann_Friedrich_Oberlin "Johann Friedrich Oberlin").

Oberlin was the home of Ernest S. Clements, a [Democratic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States) "Democratic Party (United States)") member of the [Louisiana State Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana_State_Legislature "Louisiana State Legislature") and, later, the [Louisiana Public Service Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana_Public_Service_Commission "Louisiana Public Service Commission"). He ran unsuccessfully in 1944 for [governor of Louisiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_Louisiana "Governor of Louisiana").

## Geography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Oberlin,_Louisiana&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Geography")]

According to the [United States Census Bureau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Census_Bureau "United States Census Bureau"), the town has a total area of 4.4 square miles (11.4 km 2), all land.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oberlin,_Louisiana#cite_note-Census_2010-5) Oberlin is located on [U.S. Route 165](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Route_165 "U.S. Route 165") at [LA 26](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana_Highway_26 "Louisiana Highway 26").

### 2000 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Oberlin,_Louisiana&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2000 census")]

As of the [census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Census "Census")[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oberlin,_Louisiana#cite_note-GR2-12) of 2000, there were 1,853 people, 702 households, and 464 families residing in the town. The population density was 602.0 inhabitants per square mile (232.4/km 2). There were 789 housing units at an average density of 256.3 per square mile (99.0/km 2).

The racial makeup of the town was 60.28% [White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_(U.S._Census) "White (U.S. Census)"), 37.61% [African American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_American_(U.S._Census) "African American (U.S. Census)"), 0.76% [Native American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_American_(U.S._Census) "Native American (U.S. Census)"), 0.27% [Asian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_(U.S._Census) "Asian (U.S. Census)"), 0.16% from [other races](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(United_States_Census) "Race (United States Census)"), and 0.92% from two or more races. [Hispanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_(U.S._Census) "Hispanic (U.S. Census)") or [Latino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latino_(U.S._Census) "Latino (U.S. Census)") of any race were 0.70% of the population.

There were 702 households, out of which 34.5% had children under the age of 18 living with them, 45.0% were [married couples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marriage "Marriage") living together, 17.7% had a female householder with no husband present, and 33.8% were non-families. 31.3% of all households were made up of individuals, and 13.0% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older. The average household size was 2.43 and the average family size was 3.06.

In the town, the population was spread out, with 26.4% under the age of 18, 8.0% from 18 to 24, 25.1% from 25 to 44, 24.5% from 45 to 64, and 16.0% who were 65 years of age or older. The median age was 38 years. For every 100 females, there were 90.1 males. For every 100 females age 18 and over, there were 83.8 males.

The median income for a household in the town was $23,333, and the median income for a family was $30,583. Males had a median income of $28,558 versus $16,923 for females. The [per capita income](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Per_capita_income "Per capita income") for the town was $12,050. About 18.3% of families and 25.5% of the population were below the [poverty line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poverty_line "Poverty line"), including 30.3% of those under age 18 and 31.1% of those age 65 or over.

## Education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Oberlin,_Louisiana&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Education")]

[Allen Parish School Board](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allen_Parish_School_Board "Allen Parish School Board") operates [Oberlin High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oberlin_High_School_(Louisiana) "Oberlin High School (Louisiana)") and Oberlin Elementary School in Oberlin.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oberlin,_Louisiana#cite_note-13)

There is a private school, Oberlin Covenant School, which opened circa 1986. In 1992, two people worked to operate the school, and there were five teachers who worked full time. That year, its enrollment was 40, and there were six students per teacher, a ratio lower than those of public schools.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oberlin,_Louisiana#cite_note-14)

**Oberlin** is a town in and the [parish seat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parish_seat "Parish seat") of [Allen Parish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allen_Parish,_Louisiana "Allen Parish, Louisiana"), [Louisiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana "Louisiana"), United States.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oberlin,_Louisiana#cite_note-GR6-3) As of the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), Oberlin had a population of 1,402.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oberlin,_Louisiana#cite_note-Census2020PLLede-4) The town is named after [Johann Friedrich Oberlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johann_Friedrich_Oberlin "Johann Friedrich Oberlin").

Oberlin was the home of Ernest S. Clements, a [Democratic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States) "Democratic Party (United States)") member of the [Louisiana State Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana_State_Legislature "Louisiana State Legislature") and, later, the [Louisiana Public Service Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana_Public_Service_Commission "Louisiana Public Service Commission"). He ran unsuccessfully in 1944 for [governor of Louisiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_Louisiana "Governor of Louisiana").

## Geography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Oberlin,_Louisiana&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Geography")]

According to the [United States Census Bureau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Census_Bureau "United States Census Bureau"), the town has a total area of 4.4 square miles (11.4 km 2), all land.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oberlin,_Louisiana#cite_note-Census_2010-5) Oberlin is located on [U.S. Route 165](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Route_165 "U.S. Route 165") at [LA 26](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana_Highway_26 "Louisiana Highway 26").

### 2000 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Oberlin,_Louisiana&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2000 census")]

As of the [census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Census "Census")[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oberlin,_Louisiana#cite_note-GR2-12) of 2000, there were 1,853 people, 702 households, and 464 families residing in the town. The population density was 602.0 inhabitants per square mile (232.4/km 2). There were 789 housing units at an average density of 256.3 per square mile (99.0/km 2).

The racial makeup of the town was 60.28% [White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_(U.S._Census) "White (U.S. Census)"), 37.61% [African American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_American_(U.S._Census) "African American (U.S. Census)"), 0.76% [Native American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_American_(U.S._Census) "Native American (U.S. Census)"), 0.27% [Asian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_(U.S._Census) "Asian (U.S. Census)"), 0.16% from [other races](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(United_States_Census) "Race (United States Census)"), and 0.92% from two or more races. [Hispanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_(U.S._Census) "Hispanic (U.S. Census)") or [Latino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latino_(U.S._Census) "Latino (U.S. Census)") of any race were 0.70% of the population.

There were 702 households, out of which 34.5% had children under the age of 18 living with them, 45.0% were [married couples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marriage "Marriage") living together, 17.7% had a female householder with no husband present, and 33.8% were non-families. 31.3% of all households were made up of individuals, and 13.0% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older. The average household size was 2.43 and the average family size was 3.06.

In the town, the population was spread out, with 26.4% under the age of 18, 8.0% from 18 to 24, 25.1% from 25 to 44, 24.5% from 45 to 64, and 16.0% who were 65 years of age or older. The median age was 38 years. For every 100 females, there were 90.1 males. For every 100 females age 18 and over, there were 83.8 males.

The median income for a household in the town was $23,333, and the median income for a family was $30,583. Males had a median income of $28,558 versus $16,923 for females. The [per capita income](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Per_capita_income "Per capita income") for the town was $12,050. About 18.3% of families and 25.5% of the population were below the [poverty line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poverty_line "Poverty line"), including 30.3% of those under age 18 and 31.1% of those age 65 or over.

## Education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Oberlin,_Louisiana&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Education")]

[Allen Parish School Board](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allen_Parish_School_Board "Allen Parish School Board") operates [Oberlin High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oberlin_High_School_(Louisiana) "Oberlin High School (Louisiana)") and Oberlin Elementary School in Oberlin.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oberlin,_Louisiana#cite_note-13)

There is a private school, Oberlin Covenant School, which opened circa 1986. In 1992, two people worked to operate the school, and there were five teachers who worked full time. That year, its enrollment was 40, and there were six students per teacher, a ratio lower than those of public schools.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oberlin,_Louisiana#cite_note-14)

**Assumption Parish** ([French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_language "French language"): _Paroisse de l'Assomption_, [Spanish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_language "Spanish language"): _Parroquia de la Asunción_) is a [parish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_parishes_in_Louisiana "List of parishes in Louisiana") located in the U.S. state of Louisiana. As of the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), the population was 21,039.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assumption_Parish,_Louisiana#cite_note-1) Its [parish seat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_seat "County seat") is [Napoleonville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napoleonville,_Louisiana "Napoleonville, Louisiana").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assumption_Parish,_Louisiana#cite_note-GR6-2) Assumption Parish was established in 1807, as one of the original parishes of the [Territory of Orleans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Territory_of_Orleans "Territory of Orleans").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assumption_Parish,_Louisiana#cite_note-3)

Assumption Parish is one of the twenty-two [Acadiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acadiana "Acadiana") parishes. Its major product is sugar cane. In proportion to its area, Assumption Parish produces the most sugar of any parish of Louisiana.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Assumption_Parish,_Louisiana&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

In 1807, Assumption became the eighth parish of the [Orleans Territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orleans_Territory "Orleans Territory"). Its history is rooted in its waterways and its large expanse of fertile soils ideal for farming. Settled in the middle 18th century by French and Spanish settlers, the area retains strong cultural ties to its past with conversational French still common among residents. Assumption was also a final destination for many of the French [Acadians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acadian "Acadian") exiled from [Nova Scotia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nova_Scotia "Nova Scotia") between 1755 and 1764.

In 1863 [Abraham Lincoln](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Lincoln "Abraham Lincoln") mentioned Assumption Parish in the [Emancipation Proclamation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emancipation_Proclamation "Emancipation Proclamation") as a confederate parish.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assumption_Parish,_Louisiana#cite_note-4)

## Politics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Assumption_Parish,_Louisiana&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Politics")]

Assumption Parish is represented in the [Louisiana House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana_State_Legislature "Louisiana State Legislature") by [Beryl Amedee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beryl_Amedee "Beryl Amedee"), a [Republican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)"), and [Chad Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chad_Brown_(politician) "Chad Brown (politician)"), a [Democrat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States) "Democratic Party (United States)"). During the "Solid South" era, conflicts over trade policy often caused Assumption Parish to deviate somewhat from overwhelming Democratic support, as did rebellion in the Acadiana region against [Woodrow Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodrow_Wilson "Woodrow Wilson")'s perceived hostility towards France.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assumption_Parish,_Louisiana#cite_note-22)

Since the Dixiecrat revolt, by contrast, Assumption has been a typical rural South Louisiana parish in its political behaviour. It backed Dixiecrat [Strom Thurmond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strom_Thurmond "Strom Thurmond") in 1948 and [Dwight D. Eisenhower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwight_D._Eisenhower "Dwight D. Eisenhower") in 1956 before showing powerful pro-Catholic behaviour in 1960[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assumption_Parish,_Louisiana#cite_note-23) and then turning powerfully against liberal [Midwestern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midwestern_United_States "Midwestern United States") Democrats in 1968 and 1972. With the nomination of the more centrist Southerner [Jimmy Carter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Carter "Jimmy Carter") in 1976, Assumption became again Democratic leaning until the 2000s, when, like all of the rural white South, it has turned powerfully Republican.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assumption_Parish,_Louisiana#cite_note-24)

**Assumption Parish** ([French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_language "French language"): _Paroisse de l'Assomption_, [Spanish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_language "Spanish language"): _Parroquia de la Asunción_) is a [parish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_parishes_in_Louisiana "List of parishes in Louisiana") located in the U.S. state of Louisiana. As of the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), the population was 21,039.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assumption_Parish,_Louisiana#cite_note-1) Its [parish seat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_seat "County seat") is [Napoleonville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napoleonville,_Louisiana "Napoleonville, Louisiana").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assumption_Parish,_Louisiana#cite_note-GR6-2) Assumption Parish was established in 1807, as one of the original parishes of the [Territory of Orleans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Territory_of_Orleans "Territory of Orleans").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assumption_Parish,_Louisiana#cite_note-3)

Assumption Parish is one of the twenty-two [Acadiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acadiana "Acadiana") parishes. Its major product is sugar cane. In proportion to its area, Assumption Parish produces the most sugar of any parish of Louisiana.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Assumption_Parish,_Louisiana&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

In 1807, Assumption became the eighth parish of the [Orleans Territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orleans_Territory "Orleans Territory"). Its history is rooted in its waterways and its large expanse of fertile soils ideal for farming. Settled in the middle 18th century by French and Spanish settlers, the area retains strong cultural ties to its past with conversational French still common among residents. Assumption was also a final destination for many of the French [Acadians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acadian "Acadian") exiled from [Nova Scotia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nova_Scotia "Nova Scotia") between 1755 and 1764.

In 1863 [Abraham Lincoln](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Lincoln "Abraham Lincoln") mentioned Assumption Parish in the [Emancipation Proclamation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emancipation_Proclamation "Emancipation Proclamation") as a confederate parish.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assumption_Parish,_Louisiana#cite_note-4)

During the [2010 United States census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_United_States_census "2010 United States census"), there were 23,421 people living in the parish. ## Politics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Assumption_Parish,_Louisiana&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Politics")]

Assumption Parish is represented in the [Louisiana House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana_State_Legislature "Louisiana State Legislature") by [Beryl Amedee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beryl_Amedee "Beryl Amedee"), a [Republican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)"), and [Chad Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chad_Brown_(politician) "Chad Brown (politician)"), a [Democrat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States) "Democratic Party (United States)"). During the "Solid South" era, conflicts over trade policy often caused Assumption Parish to deviate somewhat from overwhelming Democratic support, as did rebellion in the Acadiana region against [Woodrow Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodrow_Wilson "Woodrow Wilson")'s perceived hostility towards France.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assumption_Parish,_Louisiana#cite_note-22)

Since the Dixiecrat revolt, by contrast, Assumption has been a typical rural South Louisiana parish in its political behaviour. It backed Dixiecrat [Strom Thurmond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strom_Thurmond "Strom Thurmond") in 1948 and [Dwight D. Eisenhower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwight_D._Eisenhower "Dwight D. Eisenhower") in 1956 before showing powerful pro-Catholic behaviour in 1960[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assumption_Parish,_Louisiana#cite_note-23) and then turning powerfully against liberal [Midwestern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midwestern_United_States "Midwestern United States") Democrats in 1968 and 1972. With the nomination of the more centrist Southerner [Jimmy Carter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Carter "Jimmy Carter") in 1976, Assumption became again Democratic leaning until the 2000s, when, like all of the rural white South, it has turned powerfully Republican.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assumption_Parish,_Louisiana#cite_note-24)

**Assumption Parish** ([French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_language "French language"): _Paroisse de l'Assomption_, [Spanish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_language "Spanish language"): _Parroquia de la Asunción_) is a [parish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_parishes_in_Louisiana "List of parishes in Louisiana") located in the U.S. state of Louisiana. As of the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), the population was 21,039.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assumption_Parish,_Louisiana#cite_note-1) Its [parish seat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_seat "County seat") is [Napoleonville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napoleonville,_Louisiana "Napoleonville, Louisiana").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assumption_Parish,_Louisiana#cite_note-GR6-2) Assumption Parish was established in 1807, as one of the original parishes of the [Territory of Orleans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Territory_of_Orleans "Territory of Orleans").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assumption_Parish,_Louisiana#cite_note-3)

Assumption Parish is one of the twenty-two [Acadiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acadiana "Acadiana") parishes. Its major product is sugar cane. In proportion to its area, Assumption Parish produces the most sugar of any parish of Louisiana.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Assumption_Parish,_Louisiana&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

In 1807, Assumption became the eighth parish of the [Orleans Territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orleans_Territory "Orleans Territory"). Its history is rooted in its waterways and its large expanse of fertile soils ideal for farming. Settled in the middle 18th century by French and Spanish settlers, the area retains strong cultural ties to its past with conversational French still common among residents. Assumption was also a final destination for many of the French [Acadians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acadian "Acadian") exiled from [Nova Scotia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nova_Scotia "Nova Scotia") between 1755 and 1764.

In 1863 [Abraham Lincoln](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Lincoln "Abraham Lincoln") mentioned Assumption Parish in the [Emancipation Proclamation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emancipation_Proclamation "Emancipation Proclamation") as a confederate parish.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assumption_Parish,_Louisiana#cite_note-4)

## Politics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Assumption_Parish,_Louisiana&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Politics")]

Assumption Parish is represented in the [Louisiana House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana_State_Legislature "Louisiana State Legislature") by [Beryl Amedee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beryl_Amedee "Beryl Amedee"), a [Republican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)"), and [Chad Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chad_Brown_(politician) "Chad Brown (politician)"), a [Democrat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States) "Democratic Party (United States)"). During the "Solid South" era, conflicts over trade policy often caused Assumption Parish to deviate somewhat from overwhelming Democratic support, as did rebellion in the Acadiana region against [Woodrow Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodrow_Wilson "Woodrow Wilson")'s perceived hostility towards France.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assumption_Parish,_Louisiana#cite_note-22)

Since the Dixiecrat revolt, by contrast, Assumption has been a typical rural South Louisiana parish in its political behaviour. It backed Dixiecrat [Strom Thurmond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strom_Thurmond "Strom Thurmond") in 1948 and [Dwight D. Eisenhower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwight_D._Eisenhower "Dwight D. Eisenhower") in 1956 before showing powerful pro-Catholic behaviour in 1960[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assumption_Parish,_Louisiana#cite_note-23) and then turning powerfully against liberal [Midwestern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midwestern_United_States "Midwestern United States") Democrats in 1968 and 1972. With the nomination of the more centrist Southerner [Jimmy Carter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Carter "Jimmy Carter") in 1976, Assumption became again Democratic leaning until the 2000s, when, like all of the rural white South, it has turned powerfully Republican.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assumption_Parish,_Louisiana#cite_note-24)
